_meta.scope: Part A: utility/regulator filings (IRPs, riders, studies, legislation) naming microreactors or SMRs at the 16 tracked buyers' commissions and elsewhere. Part B: facility-level MW evidence for eight application loads plus two Transportation loads that data/sectors.json lists as uncited.

Ameren Missouri and Evergy/Kansas IRPs and KCC filings for SMR mentions

Part B: battery-material and battery-recycling plants (Redwood Materials, Ascend Elements, Li-Cycle, Cirba Solutions, Gopher Resource, Tesla Gigafactory Nevada) via SEC EDGAR full-text search and EIA-860M generator inventory
Part B: company-owned data centers and dedicated backup blocks (Apple Maiden NC, Meta Los Lunas NM, Thomson Reuters/West Publishing Eagan MN) via EIA-860M

absences: METHOD NOTE: WebSearch and WebFetch became rate-limited partway through this session (org session cap, reset 3pm ET) and stayed unavailable for the rest of the research window. All research after that point used direct Bash/curl fetches of known government, company and data sources (SEC EDGAR full-text API, EPA ECHO, DOE/EIA including the EIA-860M generator inventory, state legislature and PUC sites, company newsroom pages) rather than open web search. This constrained Part B especially: several loads that a search-driven pass could likely resolve went unresolved here for lack of a discovery tool, not for lack of trying.

Georgia Power's 2025 IRP (GA PSC Docket 56002, filed 2024-11-13, approved 2025-07-15) discusses nuclear uprates at Vogtle Units 1-2 and Hatch Units 1-2 (up to 112 MW combined by 2032) and says only that 'over the long-term... customers would benefit from additional new nuclear in the future' — no SMR or microreactor technology, MW or in-service year is named, so it does not qualify as an SMR/microreactor filing and was dropped rather than forced in.

Ameren Missouri: company statements (March-July 2025) say it is evaluating 'available nuclear technologies... including small modular reactors' for a future build near Callaway, but no MO PSC IRP docket number or MW figure naming an SMR was found after two search angles.

Evergy/Kansas: the 2025-09-23 TerraPower-Evergy-Kansas Department of Commerce MOU (Natrium, 345 MWe) is a state-level agreement, not yet a KCC-filed IRP supplement or docket; no KCC filing naming it was found.

Entergy Arkansas/Mississippi: the Holtec-Entergy-Hyundai SMR-300 MOA (Gulf South, ~300 MWe/unit) is a non-binding memorandum; no Arkansas PSC or Mississippi PSC filing was found (Entergy Louisiana's IRP docket, which does model SMR cost, is used instead).
Basin Electric Power Cooperative: only a May 2025 staff visit to INL's DOME testbed was found; no IRP or filing naming a microreactor or SMR.

APS/SRP/TEP: their DOE Gen III+ SMR-siting grant application was not awarded (as of early 2026); beyond the general Arizona Corporation Commission nuclear-inquiry docket (used below), no ACC filing names a specific project or MW.

Xcel Energy Colorado: company on-record position is 'We do not have plans to build nuclear in Colorado' (Colorado Sun, 2025-09-15); no CO PUC SMR docket exists despite Aurora-area (Buckley SFB) legislator interest.

West Virginia: HB 3434 and HB 5150 (2023 and 2024 sessions), which would have encouraged SMR siting at former coal sites, both stalled in committee; no enacted WV nuclear-siting statute exists to cite.

No utility-commission interconnection request, special contract or rate-case mention was found for any of the nine Janus/ANPI candidate installations (JBSA/CPS Energy, Buckley/Xcel Colorado, Malmstrom/NorthWestern, Fort Hood, Fort Bragg/Duke, Fort Campbell/TVA, Fort Benning/Georgia Power, Fort Drum/National Grid-NYPA, NWS Crane/Duke Indiana) beyond the DAF/Army selection announcements and non-binding site-characterization MOUs already on the site.

Duke Energy Indiana's 2024 IRP does not carry a confirmable IURC Cause/Docket number in any fetched primary document (one unfetched search result suggested '46155'); cited by URL only rather than risk a wrong docket number.
Iowa Utilities Commission docket/case number for MidAmerican's 2024 Resource Evaluation Study could not be independently confirmed in the fetched report itself; cited by URL only.

Part B — Battery-recycling plants: searched Li-Cycle (Rochester Hub 10-K text has no MW/power content), Redwood Materials, Ascend Elements, Cirba Solutions/Retriev, Gopher Resource, RSR Corp, INMETCO and American Battery Technology Co. in EIA-860M and SEC EDGAR; no named recycling facility with a published MW figure was found. Recorded as an absence rather than forced.

Part B — Integrated agricultural campuses combining growing, processing, refrigeration and water pumping: searched AppHarvest, Local Bounti, Superior Fresh, Little Leaf Farms, BrightFarms, Gotham Greens, Revol Greens and Lincoln Premium Poultry (Fremont, NE); none has a published facility-level MW figure reachable in this session.

Part B — Large pozzolan mines with onsite crushing, grinding or drying: searched Hess Pumice, Cemex US pozzolan/aggregate operations, US Silica, Continental Materials and St. Marys Cement in EIA-860M; none surfaced a named mine or processing site with a published MW figure.

Part B — Large rail, truck and fleet-charging hubs: searched WattEV's Bakersfield depot, Daimler Truck/Portland General Electric's 'Electric Island,' TeraWatt Infrastructure, Forum Mobility, and major rail yards (Union Pacific, BNSF) directly and in EIA-860M; none surfaced a named hub with a published MW figure in this session.

dockets.utility: Duke Energy Carolinas / Duke Energy Progress
dockets.what_it_says: Duke's 2025 Carolinas Resource Plan gives its nuclear development strategy 'optionality to choose either small modular reactors (600 megawatts by 2037) or large light-water reactors (up to 1,117 megawatts by 2037) to be deployed at the first site.' The SMR path targets Duke-owned land at the retiring Belews Creek, N.C. coal/gas station with the first SMR online in 2036; an NRC early site permit application is due Q4 2025 (permit expected 2027). Reactor technology is not yet selected, so no cost figure is given.
dockets.microreactor_read: Duke is holding a multi-unit 300 MW-class SMR option and a single large-reactor option open at the same retiring coal site, so a microreactor vendor is competing against real alternatives already in the plan, not against nothing.

sources.label: World Nuclear News — Duke Energy brings large-scale new-build into resource plan (2025-10-03)
sources.quote: small modular reactors (600 megawatts by 2037) or large light-water reactors (up to 1,117 megawatts by 2037)

sources.label: Duke Energy — 2025 Carolinas Resource Plan, Appendix J: Nuclear Highlights
sources.quote: the Companies plan to add 600 MW of advanced nuclear to the system by 2037 with the first SMR coming online in 2036

dockets.what_it_says: Duke Energy Indiana's 2024 IRP 'allowed four SMRs, sized at 300 MW each, to be selected in 2037 and each year thereafter,' at a '2024 starting capital cost... $11,150/kW' that falls under an assigned learning-rate curve by 2037. An intervenor modeling report found Duke's own least-cost model did not select any SMRs even at that assumed cost, only when they were forced into the portfolio.
dockets.microreactor_read: Indiana's own IRP economics show 300 MW-class SMRs failing to clear the utility's cost-optimized model at an $11,150/kW start cost — the number a microreactor has to beat on delivered $/kW, not just on total project price.

sources.label: Energy Futures Group — Report on Duke Energy Indiana's 2024 Integrated Resource Plan, submitted to the IURC 2025-02-13
sources.quote: Duke allowed four SMRs, sized at 300 MW each, to be selected in 2037 and each year thereafter

sources.label: Indiana Office of Utility Consumer Counselor — Comments on Duke Energy Indiana's 2024 IRP
sources.quote: Nuclear generation has many regulatory and technical hurdles while the development of small modular reactor technology continues

dockets.what_it_says: PacifiCorp's 2025 IRP (filed with all six of its state commissions: OR, WA, CA, ID, UT, WY) includes advanced nuclear in its least-cost, least-risk preferred portfolio: 'the 500 MW advanced nuclear NatriumTM demonstration project is currently scheduled to come online by the fall of 2031,' at TerraPower's Kemmerer, Wyoming site. The IRP separately references a joint PacifiCorp-TerraPower study of up to five additional Natrium units in PacifiCorp's territory by 2035.
dockets.microreactor_read: PacifiCorp has already put a specific 500 MW SMR in its resource-plan preferred portfolio with a firm target year, so a microreactor pitch here must explain why a sub-20 MW unit beats a project the utility has already committed planning capacity to.

sources.label: PacifiCorp — 2025 Integrated Resource Plan, Volume I (filed 2025-03-31)
sources.quote: the 500 MW advanced nuclear NatriumTM demonstration project is currently scheduled to come online by the fall of 2031

dockets.what_it_says: Idaho Power's 2025 IRP (also filed with the Oregon PUC) models 'a 100 MW SMR... as a selectable resource beginning in 2035,' assumed built on the Idaho National Laboratory site, citing a smaller footprint, lower capital cost and greater scalability than typical reactor designs. The unit is a candidate resource in the model, not part of the company's preferred portfolio.
dockets.microreactor_read: Idaho Power picked 100 MW as its generic SMR proxy on the INL site itself — the same site DOE is trying to fill with microreactor testbeds — so a microreactor pitch competes directly for that site's attention at a fraction of the utility's assumed unit size.

sources.label: Idaho Power — 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (filed June 2025)
sources.quote: a 100 MW SMR was modeled as a selectable resource beginning in 2035

dockets.what_it_says: MidAmerican's November 2024 Resource Evaluation Study models 'Nuclear-Small Modular Reactor' as '345 MW blocks with a book life of 40 years,' available starting 2035. A dedicated sensitivity run added 'a 345 MW SMR with 155 MW salt storage' beginning January 1, 2036, timed to follow the retirement of the Neal 3 coal unit on December 31, 2035.
dockets.microreactor_read: MidAmerican is explicitly pairing its SMR proxy with thermal storage to firm up a retiring coal unit's slot — the same firm-replacement niche a microreactor plus battery could target at a much smaller scale.

sources.label: MidAmerican Energy — Resource Evaluation Study Report (2024-11-01)
sources.quote: Nuclear small modular reactors (SMR) are modeled as 345 MW blocks with a book life of 40 years

dockets.what_it_says: NorthWestern's 2026 Montana IRP includes 'a SMR... as a candidate resource. The 320 MW size of the SMR does not represent a specific technology but is similar in size to other SMRs modeled in other IRPs... assumed to be unavailable until January 1, 2035,' positioned as a post-2035 option once the Colstrip coal plant fully retires (2043).
dockets.microreactor_read: NorthWestern picked one generic 320 MW proxy for its whole territory's nuclear line item, so a microreactor seller needs a distribution-tier story this planning process does not currently model at all.

sources.label: NorthWestern Energy — 2026 Montana Integrated Resource Plan (Docket 2025.05.038)
sources.quote: The 320 MW size of the SMR does not represent a specific technology but is similar in size to other SMRs modeled in other IRPs

dockets.utility: Xcel Energy (Northern States Power Company - Minnesota)
dockets.what_it_says: Xcel's 2024-2040 Upper Midwest Resource Plan ran an 'SMRs Only' special study in which 'SMRs are the only available advanced technology resource option for EnCompass to select starting in 2035'; that sensitivity path picks 'the first SMR... in 2047,' building to 4,200 MW of cumulative SMR capacity by 2050 and 3,000 MW more by 2055. The preferred plan itself instead extends the existing Prairie Island and Monticello nuclear plants' lives into the 2050s.
dockets.microreactor_read: Xcel's own SMR-only sensitivity doesn't pick a single SMR until 2047 — over twenty years out — which is itself the case for a microreactor a utility could deploy this decade instead.

sources.label: Xcel Energy — 2024-2040 Upper Midwest Resource Plan, Docket No. E002/RP-24-67 (filed 2024-02-01)
sources.quote: SMRs are the only available advanced technology resource option for EnCompass to select starting in 2035

dockets.what_it_says: TVA's draft 2025 Integrated Resource Plan (released 2024-09-23, comment period closed 2024-12-11) 'proposed adding up to 1 GW of nuclear capacity by 2035,' a small share of a mix otherwise dominated by up to 20 GW solar, 19 GW gas and 6 GW storage. TVA separately submitted an NRC construction-permit application for a BWRX-300 SMR at its Clinch River site (review could stretch into 2028).
dockets.microreactor_read: TVA's own systemwide IRP treats a full gigawatt of new nuclear, spread across SMR-class and larger units, as a minor share of the 2035 build-out, so a microreactor pitch to TVA has to ride on a distribution-level or federal-facility use case, not the systemwide IRP.

sources.label: Utility Dive — TVA is first US utility to apply for an SMR construction permit
sources.quote: TVA proposed adding up to 1 GW of nuclear capacity by 2035

dockets.utility: Arizona Public Service, Salt River Project, Tucson Electric Power
dockets.what_it_says: On 2025-02-07, ACC Vice Chair Nick Myers and Commissioner Rene Lopez 'opened the docket, In the Matter of the Commission's Inquiry into Nuclear Issues (Docket No. E.00000A-25-0026),' covering the possibility of new nuclear generation in Arizona, including SMRs. APS, SRP and TEP separately applied for (but were not awarded) a DOE Gen III+ SMR-siting grant and continue a joint site-screening study, with community meetings targeted for late 2026.
dockets.microreactor_read: Arizona's regulator opened a standing, technology-inclusive nuclear docket before any specific project was filed — an open door a microreactor vendor could enter directly instead of waiting for a utility RFP.

sources.label: Arizona Corporation Commission — Myers and Lopez Open Formal Inquiry into Potential New Nuclear Generation in Arizona (2025-02-12)
sources.quote: opened the docket, In the Matter of the Commission's Inquiry into Nuclear Issues (Docket No. E.00000A-25-0026)

dockets.what_it_says: Following Governor Hochul's June 2025 directive, NYPA is pursuing 'at least 1 gigawatt (GW) of advanced nuclear energy in Upstate New York': it issued two RFIs in October 2025 (drawing 23 developer/partner responses and 8 community responses) and by June 2026 was moving to an RFQ stage with Ontario Power Generation as a technical partner. No site or reactor size class has been chosen.
dockets.microreactor_read: NYPA's 1 GW program is technology- and site-open at this stage, which is exactly the window for a microreactor vendor to get evaluated before the program locks onto a single large-reactor developer.

sources.label: NYPA — Governor Hochul Announces Significant Steps in Development of at Least 1 GW of Nuclear Energy in Upstate New York (2026-06-01)
sources.quote: at least 1 gigawatt (GW) of advanced nuclear energy in Upstate New York

dockets.what_it_says: Tennessee's Nuclear Energy Fund, created in 2023 with $70 million, has been topped up each session through 2025-2026, reaching $95 million total; the 2025 session alone 'included up to $50 million in the state budget to assist in accelerating construction of small modular reactors' and to support TVA's since-successful $400 million DOE grant for a BWRX-300 SMR at the Clinch River site.
dockets.microreactor_read: Tennessee is willing to put state money directly behind SMR construction acceleration, which is the kind of state co-funding a microreactor developer siting in the same region should ask to access.

sources.label: Office of Governor Bill Lee — Tennessee Secures U.S. Department of Energy Grant to Develop Nation's First Small Modular Reactor at Clinch River Site (2025-12-02)
sources.quote: included up to $50 million in the state budget to assist in accelerating construction of small modular reactors

dockets.what_it_says: Indiana's Engrossed SB 424 amends IC 8-1-8.5-12.1 to let a public utility petition the IURC, before obtaining a certificate, to recover 'project development costs' for 'one (1) or more small modular nuclear reactors.' An approved utility 'shall recover eighty percent (80%) of the' immediately, deferring the remaining 20% to its next general rate case. Effective July 1, 2025; no utility had yet filed a petition under it as of this research.
dockets.microreactor_read: Indiana will let a utility bill ratepayers for SMR feasibility and design work before construction starts, at an 80/20 split — a template a microreactor developer could push other states to copy at a much lower absolute dollar threshold.

sources.label: Indiana General Assembly — Engrossed Senate Bill 424 (2025), SB0424.03.COMH
sources.quote: shall recover eighty percent (80%) of the

dockets.what_it_says: Entergy Louisiana's IRP filing under LPSC Docket I-37764 models new nuclear at widely divergent costs: 'SMRs are modeled at approximately $14,965/kW,' against large light-water reactors at $18,490/kW, alongside gas and renewables. No unit is selected and no in-service date is committed in the filing as reported.
dockets.microreactor_read: A microreactor developer now has a concrete Gulf South benchmark to beat: Entergy's own filed SMR cost assumption of just under $15,000/kW.

sources.label: Bayou Colline (Substack) — Gas, Nuclear, or Renewables? Entergy Louisiana's IRP Sets the Terms (2026-01-30)
sources.quote: SMRs are modeled at approximately $14,965/kW

dockets.utility: State of Utah / Office of Energy Development
dockets.what_it_says: Utah's H.B. 249, Nuclear Power Amendments (2025 General Session), creates the Nuclear Energy Consortium inside the Office of Energy Development, which 'shall: (a) provide knowledge and expertise... regarding nuclear energy technologies, safety, and development' and recommend nuclear-siting policy, plus a separate Utah Energy Council and an Electrical Energy Development Investment Fund. The consortium meets quarterly and reports annually by November 30. Effective May 7, 2025.
dockets.microreactor_read: Utah has stood up a standing state body whose job is literally to recommend nuclear-siting policy and steer an investment fund — the exact door a microreactor developer should be knocking on before a specific project docket exists.

sources.label: Utah State Legislature — H.B. 249, Nuclear Power Amendments, Enrolled Copy (2025 General Session)
sources.quote: provide knowledge and expertise to assist the office regarding nuclear energy

cases.name: Tesla Gigafactory Nevada
cases.capacity: 6.7 MW combined onsite rooftop solar PV (six generating units, EIA-860M, Aug. 2026, all Operating)
cases.summary: Tesla's Gigafactory Nevada in Storey County — the company's primary US lithium-ion battery cell and materials manufacturing site with Panasonic — reports six company-owned rooftop solar PV generating units to EIA (Plant ID 64098), ranging from 0.4 to 2 MW each, for 6.7 MW of nameplate onsite generation as of the August 2026 EIA-860M filing; all six units are listed 'Operating' (2019-2022 vintage). No CAM/precursor-specific plant (Redwood Materials, Ascend Elements, BASF, Novonix) yielded a citable facility-level MW figure in this session, so this adjacent cell/materials gigafactory is used instead; see absences.
cases.microreactor_read: Gigafactory Nevada's reported onsite generation (6.7 MW solar) is a token fraction of the plant's real electrical draw (widely reported in the hundreds of MW); the site's actual contracted load, not its onsite solar, is the number a microreactor pitch needs, and that load figure remains unpublished.

cases.name: Sierra Pacific Industries — Anderson Sawmill Cogeneration Plant
cases.capacity: 30.2 MW wood/wood-waste biomass cogeneration ('SPI Anderson 2', EIA-860M Aug. 2026, Plant ID 59658, Operating since 2015)
load: Large integrated sawmills and wood-products plants
cases.summary: Sierra Pacific Industries' integrated sawmill at Anderson, California runs an onsite 30.2 MW wood-waste biomass cogeneration unit ('SPI Anderson 2', generator GEN1, operating since 2015), one of eight SPI cogeneration plants that the company's own site says together produce 'over 180 megawatts of electrical power' from mill byproducts (bark, sawdust) — enough to run the mill and sell surplus power to local utilities.
cases.microreactor_read: A 30 MW biomass unit already profitably backs this one sawmill on effectively free fuel (mill waste); a microreactor competing for the same site has to beat that economics, not just an open-market power price.

cases.name: Archer Daniels Midland — Clinton, Iowa corn wet-milling complex
cases.capacity: 180 MW onsite coal-fired steam generation (two units, 75 MW + 105 MW; EIA-860M Aug. 2026, Plant ID 10860, both Operating since 2009)
cases.summary: ADM's Clinton, Iowa corn wet-milling and processing complex — one of ADM's largest grain-processing sites, producing sweeteners, starches and ethanol — operates two onsite conventional steam-coal generating units, 75 MW and 105 MW (180 MW combined), both reported 'Operating' in EIA's August 2026 generator inventory.
cases.microreactor_read: 180 MW is far above a single microreactor's 1-20 MW class, but it sets the scale of a large integrated mill's onsite power need; a microreactor fits better as one module in a multi-unit firm-power buildout at this class of site than as a full replacement.

cases.name: Apple — Maiden, North Carolina data center
cases.capacity: 37.5 MW company-owned onsite solar PV currently operating (20 MW + 17.5 MW across two arrays; a third 21 MW array is out of service); EIA-860M Aug. 2026
cases.summary: Apple, Inc. is the direct EIA-reported owner-operator of three onsite solar PV arrays at its Maiden, North Carolina data center campus: 'Apple Data Center - PV2' (20 MW) and 'Apple Data Center PV3' (17.5 MW) are both listed 'Operating'; a fourth, older array, 'Apple Data Center PV' (21 MW), is currently out of service. Combined operating capacity is 37.5 MW.
cases.microreactor_read: Apple already owns and directly operates generation at this campus rather than buying it through a third-party developer PPA — the same direct-ownership posture a microreactor sale to a hyperscaler's own (non-colocation) data center would need to match.

cases.capacity: 9.2 MW onsite standby diesel generation (four 2 MW units at 'West Group Data Center' plus one 1.2 MW unit at 'Thomson Reuters Data Center Bldg ES101'); EIA-860M Aug. 2026, all coded Standby/Backup

cases.summary: The West Publishing/Thomson Reuters data-center campus in Eagan, Minnesota (EIA-reported owner-operator 'CADC MSP01, LLC') reports five onsite diesel generators as dedicated outage-protection capacity: four 2 MW units at 'West Group Data Center' (8 MW) and one 1.2 MW unit at the adjacent 'Thomson Reuters Data Center Bldg ES101' — all coded '(SB) Standby/Backup: available for service but not normally used.'
cases.microreactor_read: This is a real, named, government-reported example of the category the site's own dataset otherwise treats as unsourced framing: a dedicated backup block (here, 9.2 MW of diesel) sitting inside one data-center campus, which is the load shape a microreactor-plus-battery would have to displace.
